newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL blue chips gain further but end off highs.
newsitem.headline: KL blue chips gain further but end off highs.

text.p: A 103-point surge on Wall Street provided support for Kuala Lumpur's share rally, which extended into its second post-festival session on heavy volume, dealers said on Thursday.
But the Composite Index of large-capitalisation shares lost steam by the close on profit-taking, ending up 4.68 points to 1,259.10, below its best level of 1,266.77 achieved earlier.

"I think profit-taking came in," said Ami Moris, a vice president in dealing at CapitalCorp. But she said the market should resume its rise after a breather as investors focus on second- and third-liners within the main board sector.

A weakening in utility Tenaga Nasional Bhd during the day and a decline in another key blue chip Telekom Malaysia contributed to the Composite Index's paring of gains, an institutional dealer with a local firm said.
"The downturn in the index is not entirely surprising," he said. "A number of stocks are probably already quite ripe for profit-taking."

By contrast, interest reawakened in the small-capitalisation Second Board index in the afternoon, lifting the index up 4.50 points to 618.18. Total volume was over 589 million, versus 448 million on Wednesday.
